title: CDN provider regional edge degradation breaks asset loads in EU
source_note: Failure pattern (a CDN / edge provider has a regional point-of-presence failure, so users in that region get slow or failed asset loads while origin and API paths are healthy) is a generic third-party-edge dependency class. All services, POP names, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~16:20 UTC EU users report the site looks broken - images and styles not loading. US and APAC are fine. API calls work. No deploys.

signal_lines.msg: asset load failure rate 8% in EU regions; other regions normal
EU asset load failures 35%; p95 asset latency 4s (normal ~120ms)
CDN provider status: degraded performance at FRA and AMS edge locations since 16:15 UTC
origin asset serving is healthy; API endpoints unaffected; issue is CDN-edge only, EU only
CDN provider shifted EU traffic to alternate POPs; asset latency recovering

ground_truth.root_cause: The CDN provider serving static assets had degraded performance at its Frankfurt and Amsterdam edge locations starting ~16:15 UTC (confirmed on the provider's status page). EU users experienced slow or failed asset loads - error rate up to ~35%, p95 latency ~4s - so pages rendered broken for them. The origin asset servers and all API endpoints were healthy; the problem was confined to the CDN edge in EU. Recovery came when the provider shifted EU traffic to alternate POPs.
evidence_path: rum-monitor: asset load failures rise to ~35% specifically in EU regions while other regions stay normal
CDN provider status reports degraded performance at FRA and AMS edge locations since 16:15 UTC
asset_p95_latency in EU climbs from ~120ms to ~4s
origin asset serving and API endpoints are confirmed healthy - the failure is CDN-edge only and EU only
recovery after the provider shifts EU traffic to alternate POPs
ground_truth.fix: Escalate to the CDN provider (their fix). Configure multi-CDN failover for static assets so a single provider's regional POP failure can be routed around, and keep an origin-direct fallback for critical assets.
